cards.text: The LORD told Jeremiah the prophet to write all His words in a book, because He will bring Israel and Judah home from captivity (Jer 30:2-3). Now the LORD keeps going. The people who survived the sword found favor in the wilderness, when Israel went to find rest.

cards.question: Then comes a word from the past, from when the LORD appeared. True or false: the LORD tells His people His love for them will run out someday.

cards.text: His love is everlasting, and He says, "therefore I have drawn you with loving devotion." The expired coupon I shared a junk drawer with WISHES it had that kind of shelf life.

cards.question: Then God makes promises that start with the word "Again." What does He say He'll do again for Virgin Israel?
Once Virgin Israel is rebuilt, what will she do again with her tambourines?

cards.text: Again, they'll plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria. But planting's the easy part, and anybody who ever turned around to an EMPTY cooling rack knows the real question is who gets to enjoy it.

cards.question: True or false: the farmers who plant on the hills of Samaria will get to enjoy the fruit themselves.

cards.text: Then God says a day is coming when watchmen will call out on the hills of Ephraim, the tribe named for Joseph's son (Gen 41:52; Josh 16:4). Now, watchmen yelling from a hill usually means trouble. But not this time.

cards.question: What do the watchmen on the hills of Ephraim call everyone to do?

answers.text: Go up to Zion to the LORD

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "Sing with joy for Jacob; shout for the foremost of the nations!" That's Jacob, the man God renamed Israel (Gen 35:10), and God wants this party LOUD.

cards.question: They're told to make their praises heard and say, "O LORD, ___ Your people, the remnant of Israel!"

cards.text: Then God says, "Behold, I will bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the farthest parts of the earth." The FARTHEST parts, friend. That is a long way to come home.

cards.question: True or false: God says only the strong and healthy will make the trip home.

cards.text: The blind. The lame. Expectant mothers. Women IN LABOR, on the one road trip NOBODY signs up for, and still God says, "They will return as a great assembly!"

cards.question: With the blind and the lame in the crowd, what kind of path does God say He'll make them walk?

answers.text: A level path where they won't stumble
A narrow path through the mountains
A hidden path through the desert

cards.text: They come with weeping, and God leads them beside streams of waters, for He is Israel's Father. Friend, six little cookie cutters call me Papa, and I'd hop ANY road for them, gold base and all.

cards.question: God says, "For I am Israel's Father, and Ephraim is My ___."

cards.text: Now the word of the LORD goes out to the nations, all the way to distant coastlands. The One who scattered Israel will gather them back up.

cards.question: How will the One who gathers Israel keep them?

answers.text: As a shepherd keeps his flock
As a king keeps his army
As a farmer keeps his field

cards.text: "For the LORD has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from the hand that had overpowered him." Bought back, friend, and I once had a 25 cent price sticker on me, and NOBODY ever called that a ransom.

cards.question: Once they come home and shout for joy on the heights of Zion, true or false: they'll still be scraping by with almost nothing.

cards.text: They'll be radiant over the bounty of the LORD: the grain, new wine, and oil, and the young of the flocks and herds. Radiant, friend, like the face I make when a whole batch comes out of the oven PERFECT.

cards.question: God paints a picture of their new life back home. What does He say it will be like?

cards.text: Then the dancing starts: the maidens, and young men and old as well. If the old men are out there, I'm out there too, hopping on my gold base like the oven timer just went off.

cards.question: In the middle of all that dancing, what does God say He'll turn their mourning into?

cards.text: God says He'll fill the souls of the priests abundantly, and fill His people with His goodness.
Then the LORD speaks again, and the mood changes: "A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and great weeping." It's Rachel, Jacob's wife (Gen 29:28), weeping for her children.

cards.question: Rachel weeps for her children and refuses to be comforted. Why?

cards.text: And the LORD answers her: "Keep your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for the reward for your work will come, declares the LORD."

cards.question: True or false: the LORD tells Rachel her children are gone for good.
Rachel's children will return from the land of the enemy, back to their own land. God tells her, "So there is ___ for your future."

cards.text: Then God says He has surely heard Ephraim's moaning. And Ephraim owns it: "You disciplined me severely, like an untrained calf."

cards.question: After saying God disciplined him severely, what does Ephraim ask God to do?

answers.text: Restore him so he can return
Punish the ones who hurt him
Give him a land far away

cards.text: Ephraim says after he returned, he repented, and after he was instructed, he struck his thigh in grief. That's the "oh no" slap, friend, the same one I gave myself the day I set the oven timer and never pressed start.

cards.question: True or false: Ephraim says he was ashamed because he bore the disgrace of his youth.
God calls Ephraim a precious son, a delightful child. Though God often speaks against him, what does God say He still does?

cards.text: "Therefore My heart yearns for him; I have great compassion for him," declares the LORD. That's not a boss filing paperwork on somebody, friend. That's a dad leaving the porch light on.
Then God gives directions: set up the road markers, put up the signposts, and keep the highway in mind, the road you have traveled.

cards.question: With the road markers and signposts up, what does God call Virgin Israel to do?
The road home is marked. Then God asks, "How long will you ___, O faithless daughter?"

cards.text: God says He has created a new thing in the land: "a woman will shelter a man." Then the LORD of Hosts says that when He restores them from captivity, the people of Judah will once again speak a certain word in the land.

cards.question: When God restores them, what will the people of Judah once again speak over the holy mountain?

cards.text: Judah and all its cities will dwell together in the land, the farmers and those who move with the flocks. Everybody back in the same kitchen, friend.

cards.question: God says, "for I will refresh the ___ soul and replenish all who are weak."
After all this, the prophet wakes up. True or false: he says his sleep had been restless and troubled.

cards.text: Then the prophet says, "At this I awoke and looked around. My sleep had been most pleasant to me." That's the kind of sleep you don't hit snooze to get OUT of, friend, you hit snooze to get back IN. And that's where we'll leave it for now, because the LORD isn't done talking yet.

findings.problem: The snooze joke doesn't hold together. Nobody hits snooze to get out of sleep, because snooze always means more sleep, so the contrast in 'you don't hit snooze to get OUT of' makes no sense.
